content.comment_body: Hello, I created a program for [product_name] [version_no] but I'm experiencing issues uploading it from my PC to the device. I'm unsure whether my approach is correct. This is only a portion of the program—can I use an X-connector here, or should I opt for a flag instead?

The issue appears to be that your ON/OFF delay block ([article_no]) isn't fully configured. An X-connector or flag should be connected to its output. While the simulation might function with an incomplete setup, you can't transfer it to the actual device this way.
I've attached a brief screen recording that demonstrates how to access the fault window for more detailed information.

Here is the complete program. I'm unsure whether I should use M-flags or X-connectors. This is my first project, and since the device is already installed at the customer's site, I want to ensure it operates reliably. Thank you.

It makes no major difference whether you use X-connectors or flags. If you don't require the function output of the block, you can use an X-connector at the end. I only use flags when necessary, or when all available X-connectors are already being used.
